newsitem.title: INDIA: India Maruti sees 96/97 car output at 335,000.
newsitem.headline: India Maruti sees 96/97 car output at 335,000.

text.p: India's largest passenger car maker Maruti Udyog Ltd said on Tuesday it expected 1996/97 (April-March) car output to total about 335,000 units.

"This year ending on March 31, we will produce about 335,000 vehicles," R.C. Bhargava, managing director of Maruti Udyog Ltd, told Reuters by telephone. Maruti produced 276,000 cars in 1995/96, Bhargava said.
Maruti Udyog is a 50:50 joint venture between Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp and the government of India.
"We are running almost 40 percent above capacity. At present we have a 250,000 capacity," Bhargava said.
The board of directors of Maruti met in New Delhi on Tuesday and finalised plans to expand the company's output.
The expansion will take place at the company's existing plant at Gurgaon, on the outskirts of the Indian capital, Bhargava said.
Last year Maruti had approved a 15 billion rupee ($419 million) expansion plan to add 100,000 units to the existing capacity.
"After expansion the output will go up to 350,000," Bhargava said.
He said with an expanded capacity of 350,000, the company aims to achieve a target of 500,000 cars in the year 2000.
The new capacity is expected to be commissioned by the end of 1998, company said last year.
